briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 20, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Crisis: Deepening Global Emergency
sections.content: Today, severe crisis situations due to climate change have been reported across the globe. Domestically, an emergency support camp has been activated in Geoje due to large-scale flood damage caused by climate change [4]. 'Climateflation,' driven by heatwaves and floods, is causing volatility in grocery prices and highlighting the importance of food security [2, 9]. Internationally, research has been published indicating that European oceans are 'boiling' due to record-breaking heatwaves [65, 68, 80, 85]. Summer skiing in the Alps has come to an end after 50 years [11], and Japanese farmers are shifting their farming hours to nighttime to mitigate heatwave damage [12], experiencing the unprecedented impacts of climate change firsthand. The extreme snow drought in western regions [72], the potential for deciduous changes in boreal forests [66], and warnings that the area affected by European wildfires could increase by 39% in the worst-case scenario [5, 76, 79, 83, 84, 87, 90, 97] clearly demonstrate that the climate crisis is no longer a distant future concern. Furthermore, extreme heatwaves have damaged the pitch at Paris Saint-Germain (PSG)'s home opening match, leading to an urgent relocation of the game [96].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst these crises, diverse efforts for carbon neutrality continue both domestically and internationally. Domestically, public and private entities, including the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and LG Electronics, have agreed to cooperate on creating 'sea forests' to respond to climate change [1]. Provincial education offices are continuing to expand school complex facilities, including survival swimming pools and climate change experience centers [3]. Young farmers in Daejeon are learning climate change response methods in Jeju [8], and the 'carbon-neutral AI healing industry' is rapidly growing, with related educational courses being established [6], indicating active movements towards adaptation and innovation. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism is operating 'Cell Village,' a carbon-neutral experience center utilizing characters from 'Yumi's Cells,' to encourage citizens' carbon-neutral practices [13, 14, 15, 18, 21]. The Yongin Special City Council has launched 'Carbon Neutrality Research Institute IV' [20], and Yeosu City is investing 10.7 billion KRW in supplementary budget towards carbon neutrality and urban environmental improvement [27], demonstrating the spread of practical actions for carbon neutrality across local governments, businesses, and civil society. However, concerns have also been raised that newly constructed public buildings in Incheon are going against the carbon neutrality trend [17], suggesting that continuous attention and effort are needed.

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is a core driver in responding to the climate crisis, with its foundation being strengthened both domestically and internationally. The National Assembly of the Republic of Korea has passed seven climate, energy, and environment bills for a major renewable energy transition [30, 39]. The Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) has been fully revamped after 15 years, seeking to introduce a government-led contract market and reduce generation costs [29, 31, 32, 33, 37]. Additionally, the 'Special Act on Support for Regions Affected by Coal Power Plant Closures' has passed the National Assembly [26], and policy support is being strengthened, such as granting grid priority to community-participatory renewable energy projects [40]. Canada is investing a record 70 billion Canadian dollars in renewable energy, emerging as a 'clean energy powerhouse' [44], and India is also considering low-interest loans for renewable energy producers [36], indicating active global investment in renewable energy. However, electricity demand in 2040 is projected to increase by 26.8 million kW in just four months [35, 52], and concerns have been raised that the enormous electricity demand from the AI and semiconductor industries cannot be met solely by renewable energy [41, 62]. Thus, expanding the power grid and establishing stable energy supply measures remain urgent tasks [42].

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Change Response and Controversies
sections.content: The international community continues discussions on climate change response, while demonstrating diverse approaches based on each nation's interests and circumstances. UN ESCAP has presented challenges to overcome for accelerating decarbonization in the Asia-Pacific region [53]. At COP31, a marine roadmap is being sought following record-breaking marine heatwaves [80]. China held a briefing discussing its oil and gas plans and a five-year coal plan [67], and attention was focused on President Xi Jinping's remarks regarding climate change. Meanwhile, in Florida, USA, while challenging textbook content on climate change, science education standards are being updated [63], and a report also emerged stating that climate change is reshaping Florida's population migration [64]. Debates and policy challenges surrounding climate change still exist, such as a conservative institute's challenge to the role of climate change in the Great Salt Lake's declining water levels [77, 89], and the reduction of climate change research curricula at the University of Houston [81]. Efforts to find scientific solutions are also underway, including an analysis of the role of Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology [82] and research on crustaceans regarding ocean acidification [98]. Meanwhile, energy price volatility was observed, with the domestic producer price index shifting to a decline in July for the first time in 11 months due to falling international oil prices [60].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted both the severity of the climate crisis and the diverse domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Global cooperation and swift action are more crucial now than ever. This concludes the climate briefing for August 20, 2026.
